questions.q: Why did pilot 1 say nothing about the value of the relation labels?
o: The placeholder router kept every relation, so H and Hc sent identical requests
questions.f: With the placeholder router, H and Hc were the same system: identical requests on 90 of 90 generations.

questions.q: The retrieval arms abstained on 135 of 270 generations. What does the thesis say caused it?
o: No cause is attributed; the share of the prompt and of retrieval was not separated
questions.f: The post-mortem withdrew the claim that the prompt was the main cause. Abstention tracked gold presence only weakly, and no causal split is supported.

questions.q: Why does Addendum D keep a backfill pass after the per-hop quota?
o: To raise the relevance of the list
So the cap's slots are not lost when a deeper hop is short, without removing a chosen deeper passage
To make H and Hc differ for sure
questions.f: Backfill is kept for capacity only. Addendum D claims no relevance or separability benefit, and fusion and packing can still erase the difference.

questions.q: Pilot 2 runs on the same 30 items. What is it?
o: An exposed development rerun with descriptive estimates; gate 3 is evaluated once, there
A replacement of the main run
questions.f: The protocol labels pilot 2 an exposed development rerun. Its results are sealed until the pilot closes, and no outcome-driven change may follow it.
